Results: Among the cancer types relevant to our study, lung and breast cancer showed the highest reference-adjusted RSV (RSVref: 61) in Hungary, followed by prostate (RSVref: 59), colorectal (RSVref: 52), and pancreatic cancer (RSVref: 11); whereas globally, breast cancer ranked first (RSVref: 49). RSVsens showed significant decreasing trends for all five cancer types (Mann-Kendall, all p < 0.05), with average annual percentage changes (AAPCs) of -5.39% for lung, -4.06% for breast, -3.56% for colorectal, -3.59% for prostate, and -5.23% for pancreatic cancer, respectively (all p < 0.05). Breast and prostate cancers exhibited significant (p < 0.001) and recurring seasonal peaks. During COVID-19 (vs. the pre-pandemic period), mean RSV values decreased by 10-30% across all cancers; only colorectal cancer-related campaigns were associated with a notable increase in search intensity (+66.9%, p = 0.013, q = 0.058), although this association did not remain significant after FDR correction.. Symptom-related searches predominated, whereas screening- and prevention-related queries were infrequent during the study period. Conclusions: GT may be a useful complementary tool for monitoring public interest and evaluating public health communication. The absence of consistent increases in search activity during most campaign periods, together with the predominance of symptom-related queries, suggests that current communication initiatives may have limited measurable visibility in GT search behaviour and highlights the need to strengthen communication on cancer prevention and early detection.

title: Canadian National Pancreas Conference 2025: Recent Advances in Patient-Centred Management of Pancreatic Cancer.
abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PC) is among the most lethal malignancies with slower progress in overall survival and treatment options compared to other cancers. The 2025 Canadian National Pancreas Conference (NPC)-the third biennial event of its kind-was hosted by Craig's Cause Pancreatic Cancer Society and the Baker Centre for Pancreatic Cancer in November 2025 in London, Ontario, co-organized by the Canadian Association of General Surgeons (CAGS) with accreditation through the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada. The event brought together experts across healthcare disciplines as well as researchers, students, and allied professionals to discuss the latest advances in treatment and management of this complex disease. The conference featured presentations, workshops, and discussions on the current landscape of treatment and management of PC with an emphasis on the increasing significance of genomic sequencing, equitable care, and a multidisciplinary approach.

title: Exploring Body Composition Profiles in Patients with Gastrointestinal Cancers: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the NUTRISCREEN Project.
abstract: Body composition (BC) analysis may integrate assessment of nutritional risk in patients with gastrointestinal cancers. Applying unsupervised machine learning techniques, we derived BC profiles (BCPs) and investigated their association with malnutrition risk and quality of life. This cross-sectional analysis includes gastrointestinal cancer patients enrolled in the NUTRItional and sarcopenia SCREENing project, part of the ONCOCAMP study (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06270602). Malnutrition assessment was performed using the NRS-2002, anthropometry and BC analysis; HRQoL was evaluated with the EORTC QLQ-C30 questionnaire. Principal component analysis and k-means clustering identified BCPs. Data from 189 patients (mean age: 66.3 ± 11.2 years) with gastric (37%), pancreatic (26.5%), rectal (24.3%) and hepatocellular carcinoma (12.2%) were analyzed. Overall, 36.5% of patients were at nutritional risk (NRS-2002 ≥ 3). Two BC clusters, High Muscle Profile (HMP) and Low Muscle Profile (LMP), were derived. Although no statistically significant association was observed in the overall cohort, multivariable analysis stratified by gender identified an association between LMP and nutritional risk among male patients (OR = 3.77, 95% CI: 1.08-14.3, p = 0.042); however, this finding should be considered exploratory. Nutritional risk, but not BC profiles, was associated with poorer Summary Score (β = 8.0, 95% CI: -14 to -2.3, p = 0.007) and higher Symptom Score (β = 9.8, 95% CI:4.5 to 15, p < 0.001). These preliminary results warrant further confirmation in larger, adequately powered longitudinal cohorts. Future studies should determine whether BCPs provide additional value beyond established nutritional screening and individual BC parameters in clinical practice.

title: Relationship Between Social Isolation, Loneliness, and Systemic Inflammation: A Scoping Review of Biological Signatures and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: Social isolation and loneliness are established social determinants of health, associated with 25-30% higher mortality risk, yet their relationship with systemic inflammation and broader biological and clinical outcomes has not been comprehensively synthesized across life stages. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched (2015-2025), supplemented by citation searching and a targeted supplementary search, for human studies linking social isolation, loneliness, or social connectedness to inflammatory biomarkers or biological/clinical outcomes. PRISMA-ScR guidance was followed; findings were synthesized narratively across five thematic axes as an evidence map. Of 3351 records identified, 73 studies were included. Isolation was most often associated with CRP and fibrinogen, and loneliness with IL-6. Isolation predicted sarcopenia, venous thromboembolism, pancreatic cancer, and cardiovascular disease, with inflammatory or metabolic markers mediating a modest (≈5-19%) share. Proteomic (n = 42,062) and epigenetic analyses linked loneliness to inflammatory, antiviral, and complement-pathway proteins and to accelerated epigenetic ageing; Mendelian randomization supported causal involvement of several proteins. Social connectedness and relationship quality tracked with lower IL-6 and better functional indices. Evidence was strongest in midlife and older cohorts. Social disconnection shows biologically plausible but heterogeneous associations with inflammatory and molecular signatures; harmonized measurement and prospective, hypothesis-free omics designs are needed to clarify causality and inform targeted screening.

title: Differential Prognostic Associations of Monocyte-Containing and Traditional Systemic Inflammatory Indices with Overall Survival After Resection or Palliative Bypass for Pancreatic Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Systemic inflammatory indices may differ prognostically between resectable and palliative pancreatic cancer. We compared associations of the aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR) with overall survival after pancreatic resection or palliative bypass. This single-center retrospective cohort included 240 patients treated during 2013-2023 (99 resections; 141 palliative bypasses). Indices derived from preoperative blood counts were natural-log transformed, standardized to 1 SD, and entered separately into operative-group-stratified Cox models. Group-specific associations and interactions were estimated. Reconstructed AJCC eighth-edition stage was incorporated only in the resection stratum. Interaction p values were Holm-adjusted. AISI was designated primary and SIRI key secondary. Overall, 215 deaths occurred. Median overall survival was 17.9 months after resection and 5.4 months after palliative bypass. AISI was associated with mortality following bypass (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1-SD increase in ln(AISI), 1.54; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.28-1.86) but not following resection (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.75-1.25; interaction p = 0.003; Holm-adjusted p = 0.010). SIRI showed corresponding HRs of 1.60 (95% CI, 1.30-1.96) and 0.93 (95% CI, 0.72-1.20), respectively (interaction p = 0.001; Holm-adjusted p = 0.004). Exploratory MLR analysis also showed statistical heterogeneity. SII was associated with mortality following bypass, but its operative-group interaction was not significant. The conventional NLR interaction was also nonsignificant, although model-assumption violations limited its interpretation. The AISI and SIRI findings remained robust in the sensitivity analyses. AISI and SIRI showed statistical heterogeneity in their associations with overall survival between operative groups, with higher values associated with mortality following palliative bypass. These findings do not establish that the operative procedure modifies the underlying biological relationship. The absence of pathological staging in the bypass group leaves potential residual confounding by disease extent. Independent external validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: SPP1-CD44-Mediated Crosstalk Between Endothelial and Macrophage Subpopulations Promotes Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Progression Through S100A6 Upregulation.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) progression is driven by complex cellular interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME), where endothelial cell (EC)-tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) crosstalk significantly influences angiogenesis and immune modulation, although the specific subsets and consequences remain unclear. Here, we integrated four single-cell RNA sequencing datasets (50 PDAC; 21 normal adjacent tissues) to profile EC and macrophage subpopulations, subsequently employing CellChat to decipher intercellular communication networks and identify altered ligand-receptor interactions in PDAC. Correlation and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses (TCGA-PAAD) assessed associations and prognostic value, while functional validation used EdU, CCK-8, and Transwell assays on PDAC cells. We identified a distinct endothelial subset (EC0) and macrophage subset (Mac2) with enhanced interaction signals in PDAC. This EC0-Mac2 crosstalk correlated with significant S100A6 upregulation, which was associated with poor patient prognosis. Exogenous S100A6 treatment markedly enhanced PDAC cell proliferation and migration in vitro. In conclusion, EC-Mac crosstalk may promote PDAC progression via S100A6, and this interaction pattern warrants further investigation as a candidate prognostic biomarker and potential target for disrupting stromal communication.

title: Partial regression of a refractory gastric ulcer following abdominal radiotherapy during a sofalcone-containing combination regimen.
abstract: Radiation-induced gastric ulcer is uncommon but can be persistent and difficult to heal, particularly in patients receiving ongoing multimodality cancer treatment. We report a 68-year-old man with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma who developed a refractory antral ulceration after upper abdominal radiotherapy during intermittent chemotherapy. High-dose pantoprazole, rebamipide, Kangfuxin liquid, and subsequent vonoprazan achieved bleeding control but failed to induce healing. After sofalcone was added, postprandial pain improved substantially, and serial endoscopy showed regression of the ulcer from 2.0×1.8 cm to 0.6×0.8 cm. This case highlights the therapeutic challenge of post-radiation gastric ulceration and supports further study of repair-directed therapy.

title: Blood- and Liver Stiffness-Based Non-Invasive Tests for Clinically Significant Portal Hypertension in Patients With cACLD and HCC.
abstract: The applicability of non-invasive tests (NITs) for clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is controversial. We performed a head-to-head comparison of various NITs for CSPH and evaluated rule-in/-out criteria. We conducted a retrospective study including 283 patients with HCC undergoing hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) measurement at the Vienna Hepatic Haemodynamic Lab with available, same-day data on NITs (i.e., liver stiffness measurement [LSM], platelet count [PLT], von Willebrand factor antigen [VWF:Ag], and the ratio of VWF:Ag and PLT [VITRO]). For the subsequent analysis, we focused on patients with compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD). Among 164 patients with cACLD, most were BCLC 0/A (50.6%) and CSPH prevalence was 46.3%, the median LSM was 20.0 kPa (IQR: 13.3-37.9), and mean VWF:Ag/VITRO was 266 ± 119%/2.30 ± 1.81. The VITRO score yielded the highest discriminative ability to detect CSPH (AUROC: 0.834), followed by ANTICIPATE ± NASH (AUROC: 0.822), PLT (AUROC: 0.803), LSM (AUROC: 0.779), and VWF:Ag (AUROC: 0.707). The application of the Baveno VII criterium (LSM ≤ 15 kPa & PLT ≥ 150G/L) and the VITRO score (≤ 1.0) individually showed an excellent performance for ruling-out CSPH (sensitivities: ≥ 95%, NPV: 100%/87.9%). For ruling-in CSPH by individual criteria, the VITRO score provided the highest PPV (≥ 2.5, specificity/PPV: 89.8%/83.0%), followed by the Baveno VII criteria (specificity/PPV: 81.8%/74.6%). When sequentially applying Baveno VII criteria and VITRO, the grey zone could be significantly reduced to 16% (sensitivity/NPV: 94.7%/92.2%; specificity/PPV: 73.9%/84.4%). The discriminative ability in patients with cACLD and HCC was comparable to patients without HCC. However, PPVs of established criteria were < 90%, which may be explained by the comparatively low prevalence of CSPH in this context.
journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

title: From Choledocholithiasis to Metastatic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: A Diagnostic Odyssey Highlighting Missed Red Flags.
abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is one of the deadliest types of cancer, with a very gloomy prognosis, especially if the cancer is at an advanced stage at the time of diagnosis. Among young adults, the vague symptoms that are usual with pancreatic cancer can be confused with those of a benign biliary condition, so the diagnosis is often late. It may be quite challenging to recognize that a bile duct obstruction with jaundice is due to a periampullary tumor, which is similar to a bile duct stone, unless one suspects it very strongly. We present the case of a 38-year-old man who suffered from increasing abdominal pain, significant weight loss, and obstructive jaundice. An initial triphasic CT showed the presence of dilated intrahepatic biliary ducts and a dilated common bile duct (CBD) with duodenal spots that were thought to be passed gallstones. At the same time, a liver lesion was identified as a probable hemangioma. The diagnosis was postponed even though the liver function tests were progressively deteriorating (total bilirubin increased to 10.4 mg/dL and alkaline phosphatase to 1394 U/L). Further endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) revealed a distal CBD stricture without stones; therefore, a plastic stent was placed. No tissue sampling was obtained during ERCP. Five months later, an extremely high carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA 19-9) (>500 U/mL) and a repeat triphasic CT showed a 43 × 45 mm pancreatic head tumor with liver and lung metastases. These findings supported a clinical-radiological diagnosis of metastatic pancreatic malignancy, presumed pancreatic adenocarcinoma; histopathological confirmation of the pancreatic or hepatic lesions was not obtained. Subsequent ascitic fluid cytology showed malignant cells consistent with adenocarcinoma, but immunocytochemistry was not available, so the pancreatic primary was not independently established. This case highlights that if a biliary stricture occurs without a stone that can be identified in a patient with progressive obstructive jaundice, the stricture should be considered malignant until demonstrated otherwise. Early obtaining of tissue for diagnosis and appropriate use of tumor markers as supportive rather than definitive tests are the main elements to steer clear of a long diagnostic odyssey.

title: Pancreatic Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasm in a Carrier of a Reported Pathogenic BRCA2 Variant: Diagnostic Considerations and Management Using European and International Guidelines.
abstract: Pathogenic germline variants in BRCA2 are associated with increased susceptibility to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and may prompt pancreatic surveillance in selected high-risk individuals. Whether BRCA2 status increases the prevalence or alters the biological behavior of intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) remains uncertain. We report a 71-year-old Latin American woman with a reported heterozygous pathogenic BRCA2 variant and a remote history of stage IA hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast carcinoma. The original molecular genetics report was unavailable; therefore, the exact variant designation, testing platform, laboratory classification, and American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG)/Association of Molecular Pathology (AMP) evidence could not be independently verified. In June 2025, during long-term oncologic follow-up, positron emission tomography-computed tomography incidentally identified a 21×21 mm pancreatic tail cyst. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) in July 2025 demonstrated a 22×20 mm cyst communicating with the main pancreatic duct (MPD), which measured 5 mm. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) demonstrated a 20×23 mm septated cyst without mural nodules or a solid component. Serum carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA 19-9) was 21.4 U/mL. Cyst fluid glucose was 12 mg/dL, amylase 316 U/L, and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) 247 ng/mL. Cytologic examination and an adequate cell-block specimen obtained by EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) demonstrated papillary mucinous epithelium with gastric-type features, favoring a low-grade IPMN. No immunohistochemical studies were performed, and the specimens were evaluated by a gastrointestinal pathologist. The case was reviewed by a multidisciplinary team in August 2025. The 5 mm MPD represented a relative indication for surgery under the 2018 European evidence-based guidelines and a worrisome feature under contemporary international criteria, but no absolute or high-risk indication for resection was identified. Surveillance was selected. Computed tomography (CT) in December 2025 showed a stable 22×20 mm cyst and a 5 mm MPD; serum CA 19-9 was 24.7 U/mL. In May 2026, the cyst measured 22×21 mm, and the MPD remained 5 mm. The patient remained clinically stable and asymptomatic without pancreatitis, obstructive jaundice, abdominal pain, weight loss, or other symptoms attributable to the lesion. This case illustrates the integration of lesion-specific morphology, ductal anatomy, pathology, longitudinal imaging, and hereditary-risk context without using reported BRCA2 status alone as an indication for pancreatic resection.

title: Ultrasound-Mediated Modulation of circRNA hsa_circ_0004870 as a Prognostic and Therapeutic Biomarker in Pancreatic Cancer.
abstract: Pancreatic cancer remains one of the most fatal tumors, with a 5-year survival rate of less than 10%, owing mostly to late-stage detection and inadequate treatment efficiency. The pressing need for novel diagnostic and therapeutic approaches has sparked interest in genetic biomarkers and ultrasound-based precision therapies. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have recently been identified as intriguing regulatory molecules with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic applications. A comprehensive study of transcriptome and clinical datasets revealed that hsa_circ_0004870 is significantly elevated in pancreatic cancer tissues and is linked with poor patient outcomes. Functional tests, including colony formation, cell counting kit-8, flow cytometry, wound healing, and Transwell invasion studies, were used to evaluate its biological roles. Bioinformatic predictions, along with dual-luciferase reporter assays, revealed the hsa_circ_0004870/miR-3124-3p/TRIM24 regulatory axis. In vivo xenograft research and immunohistochemistry analyses supported these findings. In addition, the authors developed an ultrasound-mediated biophysical modulation model to investigate the potential therapeutic control of this axis. hsa_circ_0004870 was highly overexpressed in pancreatic cancer cells, which increased proliferation, migration, and invasion. It acts as a competitive endogenous RNA, sequestering miR-3124-3p, resulting in increased TRIM24 and tumorigenic behavior. In vivo, silencing hsa_circ_0004870 reduced tumor development significantly. Combining these findings with developments in ultrasound-targeted gene and molecular delivery technology suggests that ultrasound-mediated manipulation of the hsa_circ_0004870 axis might provide a precise and noninvasive therapeutic method to overcome resistance and enhance localized cancer management. hsa_circ_0004870 was overexpressed in pancreatic cancer cells, resulting in enhanced proliferation, migration, and invasion. It works as a competitive endogenous RNA, sequestering miR-3124-3p, leading to enhanced TRIM24 and tumorigenic behavior. In vivo, suppressing hsa_circ_0004870 dramatically decreased tumor growth. Combining these findings with advances in ultrasound-targeted gene and molecular delivery technology, it appears that ultrasound-mediated manipulation of the hsa_circ_0004870 axis could provide a precise and noninvasive therapeutic method for overcoming resistance and improving localized cancer management.

title: NCLX Inhibition plus Ca<sup>2+</sup> Delivery Potentiates Electroporation and Antitumor Immunity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Irreversible electroporation (IRE) is increasingly used for locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet electric-field heterogeneity leaves a low-field rim where residual cells survive, and recurrence is frequent, compounded by a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, an electroporation-synchronized adjuvant strategy is developed that integrates intratumoral Ca<sup>2+</sup> delivery with nanoparticle-mediated inhibition of mitochondrial NCLX using CGP37157 (mPEG-PCL@CGP37157). This regimen markedly enhances cytotoxicity in PDAC cell lines and patient-derived organoids and significantly improves local control and survival in syngeneic subcutaneous and orthotopic PDAC models, without overt systemic toxicity. Reduced therapeutic efficacy in T cell-deficient hosts demonstrates the importance of adaptive immunity. Mechanistically, EP-resistant PDAC cells upregulate NCLX to buffer mitochondrial Ca<sup>2+</sup> stress. Concurrent Ca<sup>2+</sup> delivery and pharmacological NCLX inhibition induce sustained mitochondrial Ca<sup>2+</sup> overload, triggering immunogenic GSDMD-dependent pyroptosis. This is accompanied by enhanced dendritic cell activation and CD8<sup>+</sup> T-cell responses, as well as suppression of a tumor-myeloid SPP1-CD44 axis, promoting pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization. Collectively, targeting NCLX potentiates the immunogenic effects of IRE and provides a translatable strategy for eliminating residual disease in PDAC.

title: Network analysis of the relationship between anxiety, depression and resilience in patients with pancreatic cancer and gender differences.
abstract: Pancreatic cancer patients demonstrate elevated vulnerability to depression and anxiety relative to other gastrointestinal malignancies, attributable to the disease's dismal prognosis and substantial symptom burden. However, symptom-level relationships among anxiety, depression, and resilience in pancreatic cancer remain insufficiently understood. Therefore, this study employed network analysis to investigate the interrelationships among anxiety, depression, and psychological resilience in the population. Additionally, a comparative analysis of the network structure was conducted to explore gender differences. Ultimately, this study aims to provide theory-driven intervention strategies and practical guidelines for supporting the mental health of patients diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. This cross-sectional study enrolled 759 patients with pancreatic cancer from Guangzhou, China, between June 2024 and July 2025. Anxiety, depression, and resilience were assessed using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) and Brief Resilience Scale (BRS). A regularized partial correlation network was constructed based on the survey data, and the bridge expected influence index was applied to quantify the bridge components. We also compared the network structures of male and female samples to explore sex differences. The prevalence rates of anxiety and depression were 24.2% and 30.3%, respectively. A7 "Panic" (0.903) was the core symptom in the anxiety, depression, and resilience symptom networks. R1 "Bounce back quickly" (-3.342) was the core bridge symptom connecting the three network clusters. A comparison of male and female networks indicated that the overall network structure exhibited no significant sex differences; however, the global strength of the female network was significantly higher. The strongest positive associations remained consistent across the male and female networks (R1 "Bounce back quickly" and R3 "Recover from stress quickly"). A7 "Panic" emerged as a shared core symptom in both male and female networks. "Panic" was identified as the central symptom in the anxiety-depression-resilience symptom networks, while "Bounce back quickly" served as the key bridge node connecting these three symptom clusters. These findings provide potential symptom-level targets for future psychological assessments and intervention research. Additionally, there were significant differences in global strength between male and female networks, with gender-specific strategies recommended for each.

title: [Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Tissue Acquisition of Pancreatic Solid Tumors].
abstract: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition for pancreatic solid tumors has become essential in diagnostic practice. Although endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) has demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy, its cytology-based samples often limit histologic evaluation, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing. To overcome these limitations, end-cutting fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB) needles-notably Franseen and fork-tip designs-were developed to obtain well-preserved core tissue. These needles improve diagnostic accuracy, tissue adequacy, and sampling efficiency compared with FNA or reverse-bevel devices. Technical refinements have also improved outcomes. Fanning and torque maneuvers enhance tissue sampling across heterogeneous tumors, while aspiration strategies such as slow-pull, wet suction, and heparinized wet suction optimize core tissue preservation and reduce blood contamination. Macroscopic on-site evaluation confirms specimen adequacy, often reducing required needle passes without cytopathology support. Although generally safe, endoscopic ultrasound-guided sampling may cause bleeding, infection, pancreatitis, or rare needle-tract seeding. Careful needle selection, minimizing needle passes, and attention to anatomical relationships are crucial to mitigating these risks. Current evidence does not support routine prophylactic antibiotic use for solid lesions. As precision oncology increasingly relies on molecular profiling and next-generation sequencing, reliable procurement of high-quality tissue has become more important. This review summarizes advances in needle design, sampling techniques, on-site evaluation, antibiotic considerations, and complication management in endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue sampling of pancreatic solid tumors.

title: Paraganglioma and childhood-onset optic atrophy in a SDHA compound heterozygous patient: an example of dual dominant and recessive inheritance.
abstract: SDHA pathogenic variants cause moderate to severe complex II deficiency, which manifests as a mitochondrial disorder in a homozygous/compound heterozygous child, or as hereditary cancer, mostly paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma, in a heterozygous adult. Here, we report the first composite heterozygous SDHA patient (hypomorphic allele p.(Thr508Ile) × null allele p.(Arg451His)) who developed complete congenital optic atrophy and a paraganglioma at the age of 36 yrs. No other germline variants were identified by sequencing panels of genes involved in these two disorders. This raises the question of whether paraganglioma screening should be implemented for carriers of a null SDHA variant.

title: Regorafenib induces ferroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma via the EGFR-TNF/NF-κB signaling axis.
abstract: Regorafenib is a standard second-line multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor for sorafenib-resistant hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Ferroptosis is a promising therapeutic cell-death modality, but the upstream signaling events governing regorafenib-induced ferroptosis remain unclear. We examined regorafenib activity in treatment-naive SNU-449 and HuH-7 HCC cells and mouse tumor models using ferroptosis-related assays, including reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), labile Fe<sup>2+</sup>, lipid peroxidation and mitochondrial ultrastructure. Transcriptome profiling was integrated with genetic and pharmacological modulation of EGFR and p65. Antitumor effects were assessed in HuH-7 xenografts and Hepa1-6 syngeneic tumors. Regorafenib suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth, with reduced Ki-67 expression. It downregulated SLC7A11/xCT and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and increased ROS, labile Fe<sup>2+</sup>, lipid peroxidation, and MDA; ferrostatin-1 partially restored viability and attenuated lipid peroxidation. Transcriptome analysis identified enrichment of the TNF signaling pathway. Regorafenib reduced total and phosphorylated EGFR and p65, decreased the p-EGFR/EGFR and p-p65/p65 ratios, and inhibited p65 nuclear translocation. p65 knockdown decreased SLC7A11/xCT and GPX4 and intensified ferroptosis, whereas p65 overexpression attenuated these effects. EGFR knockdown reduced TNF-α and enhanced ferroptosis; the EGFR agonist NSC228155 restored NF-κB activity and SLC7A11/xCT-GPX4 expression. Combined EGFR knockdown and lenalidomide treatment further enhanced ferroptosis-associated phenotypes in vitro. Exploratory analysis of 24 paired specimens showed EGFR, p65, and GPX4 were upregulated and positively associated. These findings identify EGFR-TNF/NF-κB signaling as a functional upstream module in treatment-naive HCC models and support validating combined EGFR knockdown and lenalidomide treatment in resistant models.

title: Negative-Pressure Fixation Improves RNA Preservation and Increases the Success Rate of the Oncomine Dx Target Test in Lung Cancer Formalin-Fixed Paraffin-Embedded Samples.
abstract: Genetic tests for lung cancer, such as the Oncomine Dx Target Test (ODxTT), are essential for patient management, and require RNA and DNA of sufficient quality and quantity from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples. ODxTT fails due to poor nucleic acid preservation. Although enhancing the penetration of formalin into tissues improves nucleic acid preservation, the clinical utility of negative-pressure fixation methods remains unclear. Therefore, we investigated whether the negative-pressure fixation method using a vacuum fixation device improves ODxTT success rates and the quality of nucleic acids in FFPE samples from lung and other cancers, and examined the underlying mechanisms. The ODxTT success rate was higher with the negative-pressure fixation method than with the conventional method (96.5% vs. 81.2%), accompanied by increased RNA quality and yield; however, no marked differences were observed in DNA. RNA deteriorated more rapidly than DNA in resected mouse liver tissues, indicating that RNA is more labile than DNA during cold ischemia. Furthermore, in FFPE samples from colon, pancreatic, and prostate cancers, negative-pressure fixation consistently improved RNA DV200. These results indicate that the negative-pressure fixation method improves ODxTT success by accelerating formalin penetration, which may suppress RNase-mediated RNA degradation and preserve RNA quality.

title: Prevention and management of hormonal crisis in neuroendocrine tumors undergoing PRRT (peptide receptor radionuclide therapy): a systematic review.
abstract: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) is an established treatment of advanced well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) expressing somatostatin receptors. Although generally well tolerated, PRRT may precipitate or exacerbate pre-existing hormonal syndromes in patients with functioning NETs, leading to acute endocrine decompensation requiring urgent management. Current recommendations from the most important NET societies for prevention and treatment remain inconsistent, and available evidence is still fragmented. To address this gap, we conducted a comprehensive systematic review of the literature in PubMed, Scopus, and Embase up to May 2025, with the aim of identifying, organizing, and critically appraising the existing evidence on prevention and therapeutic strategies for managing hormonal crises in patients undergoing PRRT. Twenty-eight studies were included, comprising 18 case reports/series, 7 retrospective studies, and 3 prospective studies. Reported events included carcinoid crisis, insulinoma-related hypoglycemia, VIPoma-related secretory crisis, ectopic Cushing syndrome exacerbation, and catecholaminergic crisis in pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma. Carcinoid crisis was the most frequently reported endocrine emergency, with available cohort studies suggesting an incidence ∼1% during PRRT, although definitions and reporting remain heterogeneous. Hypoglycemic crises occurred mainly during the first PRRT cycle in patients with insulinoma, supporting the role of inpatient monitoring and preventive glucose-stabilizing strategies. Evidence for rarer syndromes was limited to small series and case reports but consistently emphasized pretreatment endocrine optimization, syndrome-specific prophylaxis, early recognition, and multidisciplinary management. Overall, available data remain insufficient to support firm recommendations but suggest that structured risk assessment, periprocedural monitoring, and harmonized management algorithms are essential to improve PRRT safety in functioning NETs.
